title: Microsoft Purview — DLP, Sensitivity Labels & Retention
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (information protection program across Microsoft Purview: sensitivity labels + auto-labeling, DLP policies, retention/records; multi-service, org-wide data governance).
hook: Classify, protect, and retain your data with Microsoft Purview — the right way
problem: Sensitive data leaks and compliance gaps almost always trace back to the same root: data that isn't classified, protected, or retained. Microsoft Purview fixes that — but rolled out carelessly, labels confuse users, DLP floods the help desk with false positives, and retention either deletes too much or nothing at all. This solution gives you a repeatable way to implement Microsoft Purview information protection: a sane sensitivity-label taxonomy with auto-labeling, DLP policies that start in audit and tune before they enforce, and retention/records that meet compliance without surprises.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the Purview information-protection model (sensitivity labels + label policies + auto-labeling, DLP across M365/endpoints, retention labels/policies and records management), and how they work together.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Microsoft 365 + Purview licensing, Entra ID, a label taxonomy, data owners, a pilot scope, change control) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: design the label taxonomy, publish labels and label policies, configure auto-labeling, build DLP policies in audit and tune, set retention labels/policies and records, pilot, validate, then expand.
5 PowerShell scripts — Purview configuration discovery, label/DLP/retention coverage validation, a classification + DLP-event report, safe remediation of gaps, and a protection-scope group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: A repeatable way to implement Microsoft Purview information protection — a sane sensitivity-label taxonomy with auto-labeling, DLP policies tuned in audit before enforcement, and retention/records that meet compliance. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
